title.quote:
# Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial
**Official title:** Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial

design.value: 2-arm, multicenter, randomized clinical trial; registered as INTERVENTIONAL with RANDOMIZED allocation, SINGLE masking and TREATMENT as primary purpose
design.quote: is a 2-arm, multicenter, randomized clinical trial designed to test whether a treatment program aimed at reducing systolic blood pressure (SBP) to a lower goal than currently recommended will reduce cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk.
design.location: Brief summary; allocation and masking in Registry identity

phase.value: NA (as recorded in the mutable-fields block observed 2026-08-13T17:02:18.930Z)
phase.location: Mutable fields — observed 2026-08-13T17:02:18.930Z from the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2

n.location: Mutable fields — observed 2026-08-13T17:02:18.930Z from the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2

n_description.value: Registry-reported enrollment of 9361, flagged ACTUAL, as observed on 2026-08-13T17:02:18.930Z from the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2. This is a registry enrollment figure, not a published analysis population; the posted adverse-event denominators are 4678 (Intensive) and 4683 (Standard).
n_description.location: Mutable fields — observed 2026-08-13T17:02:18.930Z from the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2

population.value: Participants aged at least 50 years with systolic blood pressure of 130 mm Hg or above (130-180 mm Hg depending on number of antihypertensive medications) and at least one additional CVD risk factor; diabetes mellitus and history of stroke were exclusions
population.quote: SPRINT strived to enroll about 9250 participants aged ≥ 50 years with SBP ≥130 mm Hg and at least one additional CVD risk factor.
population.location: Detailed description; entry thresholds and exclusions in Eligibility

followup.value: Participants were followed for 4-6 years; registered outcome time frames are 6 years, except the Small Vessel Cerebral Ischemic Disease outcome at 4 years
followup.quote: Participants were recruited at approximately 90 clinics within 5 clinical center networks (CCNs) over approximately a 2-year period, and were followed for 4-6 years.

intervention.value: Intensive control of SBP to a goal of SBP <120 mm Hg using one or more study-provided antihypertensive drug classes, titrated at monthly visits
intervention.quote: - **DRUG: Intensive control of SBP** — Participants in the Intensive arm have a goal of SBP \<120 mm Hg. Use of once-daily antihypertensive agents will be encouraged unless alternative frequency is indicated/necessary.

comparator.value: Standard control of SBP to a goal of SBP <140 mm Hg using the same medications (registered as ACTIVE_COMPARATOR)
comparator.quote: - **DRUG: Standard control of SBP** — Participants in the Standard BP arm have a goal of SBP \<140 mm Hg. The same medications used in the Intensive BP arm will be used for the Standard BP arm.

limitations: Back-transformation of the inverse hyperbolic sine transformed white matter lesion volumes to the original cm3 scale is difficult, as the record itself states for the Small Vessel Cerebral Ischemic Disease outcome

risk_of_bias.judgement: The trial is registered with SINGLE masking for an open-label blood-pressure treat-to-target intervention, so participants and treating clinicians knew the assigned SBP goal.
risk_of_bias.quote:
- **Study type:** INTERVENTIONAL

- **Allocation:** RANDOMIZED

- **Masking:** SINGLE

- **Primary purpose:** TREATMENT

risk_of_bias.judgement: The blood pressure intervention was stopped earlier than originally planned in order to disseminate significant preliminary results, which can inflate effect estimates and truncates follow-up for the cognitive outcomes.
risk_of_bias.quote: NIH stopped the blood pressure intervention earlier than originally planned in order to quickly disseminate the significant preliminary results.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The Small Vessel Cerebral Ischemic Disease outcome rests on 449 of the 670 participants with a baseline white matter lesion measurement, a loss of roughly one third of the imaging substudy.
risk_of_bias.quote: Of the 670 participants with WML volume measurement at baseline, 462 completed the follow-up MRI. Image quality control requirements were not met for 13 participants with a follow-up MRI scan, resulting in a sample of 449 adults.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The all-cause dementia outcome is reported only among participants who completed at least one cognitive assessment during follow-up, not among all randomized participants.
risk_of_bias.quote: Population: Participants who completed at least 1 cognitive assessment during follow-up
